headline: JaSaD President Inu sentenced to 10 years in jail for crimes against humanity
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced the political leader for his role in the killing of six people in Kushtia.
details: JaSaD President Inu has been sentenced to 10 years in prison by the International Crimes Tribunal.
The verdict comes in a case involving crimes against humanity, specifically the killing of six people in Kushtia.
The tribunal delivered the judgment on Tuesday, bringing a conclusion to the legal proceedings against the political leader.
Inu was brought to the tribunal under heavy security as the court prepared to announce the verdict.
caption:

headline_marked: 1,500 cases filed as [[AI cameras monitor Dhaka traffic]]
headline: 1,500 cases filed as AI cameras monitor Dhaka traffic
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police have expanded AI surveillance to 19 intersections to detect violations and reduce congestion.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed announced that approximately 1,500 traffic violation cases have been filed using AI cameras during their first two months of operation.
The system has now been expanded to 19 intersections across the capital, including four new locations in Mohammadpur, to improve traffic management and road safety.
The AI cameras are programmed to detect various violations of the Road Transport Act 2018, such as speeding, dangerous lane changes, and failure to wear helmets.
Despite the new technology, DMP revealed that around 38,000 traffic summons remain pending, largely due to outdated vehicle ownership records causing delivery complications.
Digital traffic cases are currently being sent to vehicle owners via mail, reducing the need for police officers to stop vehicles manually on the road.
Commissioner Ahmed stated that the system has already led to visible improvements, with drivers showing a greater tendency to stay in their lanes and obey traffic signals.
caption:
AI is now watching Dhaka's roads. 1,500 cases have already been filed through automated surveillance.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed announced that approximately 1,500 traffic violation cases have been filed using AI cameras during their first two months of operation.

The system has now been expanded to 19 intersections across the capital, including four new locations in Mohammadpur, to improve traffic management and road safety.

The AI cameras are programmed to detect various violations of the Road Transport Act 2018, such as speeding, dangerous lane changes, and failure to wear helmets.

Despite the new technology, DMP revealed that around 38,000 traffic summons remain pending, largely due to outdated vehicle ownership records causing delivery complications.

Digital traffic cases are currently being sent to vehicle owners via mail, reducing the need for police officers to stop vehicles manually on the road.

Commissioner Ahmed stated that the system has already led to visible improvements, with drivers showing a greater tendency to stay in their lanes and obey traffic signals.

#Dhaka #TrafficPolice #SmartCity #Bangladesh #RoadSafety

Source: bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo
